judged_text: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but its callers destructure provider-specific shapes: Google does `res?.data` (googleauth result shape) and Hubspot/Zoho-Bigin treat the return value as a parsed token/axios response. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, Google's `token.access_token` throws TypeError (Response has no `.data`), and Hubspot/Zoho-Bigin read undefined token fields and persist undefined/NaN expiry into credential rows — token refresh is broken and can destroy stored credentials for every sync-mode deployment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, does `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns that raw `Response` object (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Callers still assume provider-specific return shapes: GoogleCalendarService assigns `const token = res?.data` and then reads `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), which will fail because a fetch `Response` has no `.data`. Hubspot and Zoho-Bigin similarly treat the return as a parsed token/axios response (`HubspotToken` and `tokenInfo.data...`), but in sync mode they will receive a `Response` without those fields, breaking refresh and potentially leading to bad persistence paths when those undefined fields are used downstream.
